data: 308 trials, 20 subjects (S_001..S_027), conditions aided (155 trials) / unaided (153); EEG 1024 Hz, 32 scalp channels (EXG1/EXG2 mastoids are misc, not picked); stimulus = shipped 44.1 kHz wav (band-limited ~4.05 kHz)
repo_validator_cli: python -m cnsp_datasets.validate vanheusden2020 --standardised-dir <std> --first-attended --picks eeg --reference average --n-subjects 0 (per condition: same validate() call on the records of one condition, scripts/run_validator.py)

pass_criteria.low: population mean r above the circular-shift null (p_circ < 0.05) and the mismatched-stimulus null (p_mismatch < 0.05); p floors 1/51 = 0.0196 and 1/21 = 0.0476
pass_criteria.mlr: population mean SNR (RMS 18-45 ms / RMS -75..-20 ms, 30-60 Hz, half-wave-rectified audio) above 100 circular-shift nulls, p < 0.05 (floor 1/101 = 0.0099)
pass_criteria.cumulative: a tier counts only if all lower tiers pass
pass_criteria.subject_level: subject tier: low if subject p_circ and p_mismatch < 0.05; mlr/brainstem if the subject's permutation p < 0.05 (cumulative)

sanity.note: neural trials are 0-12 ms shorter than the stimulus at 64 Hz rounding (ceil at 1024 Hz vs wav); no unit, flat or NaN flags; no channels marked bad

lag_sweep.status: MISSING in the repo validator: no global stimulus-shift sweep against a fixed model. The closest repo output is the per-trial peak shift (+-0.5 s, parabolic) of each held-out trial against the subject model trained on the other trials; a constant offset common to all trials is absorbed by that model and cannot be seen. Tolerance: none defined in the repo; compared here with 1 sample at 64 Hz (15.6 ms) as in earlier reports.
lag_sweep.within_tolerance: yes: population median +0.76 ms pooled (bootstrap 95% -1.40..+1.70), aided +0.20, unaided -0.30; every subject median within +-12.5 ms
lag_sweep.jitter_sd_note: SD is not robust: weak trials land at the +-500 ms search edge, and aided S_014 trial 9 (first of its 2nd recording) has an offset of -19470 ms (outside the +-500 ms range: the parabolic step in models.peak_shift is unbounded when the curvature is near zero), which drives the aided SD to 1562 ms
lag_sweep.explorer_absolute_check: notes.md 6: leave-one-subject-out lag peak -20..+24 ms, aided mean 0.0 ms, unaided -1.4 ms (explorer script, not the repo validator)

latency_trf.method: repo low-tier forward TRF (0.5-8 Hz envelope, 64 Hz, all trials of the subject), GFP over 32 channels / median circular-null GFP; N1 = max in 50-150 ms, P2 = max in 150-300 ms. The validator stores the GFP only (no signed channel TRFs), so N1/P2 polarity cannot be checked: these are GFP maxima, 15.6 ms grid
latency_trf.note: the grand GFP has one dominant peak at 172 ms (pooled GFP/null 8.8) with local maxima near 0 ms (4.6) and 78 ms (3.9); the 'N1' value at 141 ms is the window edge on the rising flank of the 172 ms peak, not a separate maximum. Separate N1/P2 latencies are not resolvable from the repo output

brainstem_band_gfp_peak_ms.note: no peak in 4-9 ms (GFP/null ~1.0); the 30-250 Hz maxima sit at 24-45 ms, i.e. middle-latency content

provenance_note: order_ambiguous trials score lower (median r 0.034, n 41, vs 0.058, n 267; Mann-Whitney p 3e-7), as expected because these files were flagged for weak tracking; 38/41 have r > 0; the r <= 0 ones are S_004 aided odin_1_2 (-0.013), S_017 unaided odin_1_2 (-0.0005), S_019 unaided slot 2 odin_1_2 (-0.0008, an ambiguous slot). All ambiguous files except S_004 aided pass low at the subject level. S_004 unaided (ambiguous) scores r 0.069 at the p floors, higher than notes.md's 'no usable tracking'. S_002 unaided (EEG-derived order 1_3,1_4,1_1,1_2) scores r 0.102, the highest of the 40 subject-conditions (trials 0.067-0.125); its order was chosen on EEG, so this is partly circular, but no trial is weak

pooled_model_trial_offsets_ms.method: per-trial peak shift against the pooled (both-condition) subject model; per subject median aided minus median unaided

all_20.note: S_004 aided median -283 ms (weak file) dominates the mean

pooled_model_trial_offsets_ms.interpretation: no measurable hearing-aid delay; the point estimate has the opposite sign of an aid delay (aided would fit later = positive) and is within the 64 Hz resolution

aided_vs_unaided.per_condition_offsets_note: per-condition offsets are relative to each condition's own model, so their difference cannot show a delay; listed in aided_vs_unaided.trial_offset_median_ms for completeness

trial_validation_tier_rule: per trial = population tier of its condition (both conditions: mlr)

reference_datasets.note: hand-aligned reference datasets, same repo validator (forward model, mean r over channels)

missing_checks: backward (decoder) model for the low tier: the repo validator fits a forward model only
global lag sweep with a defined tolerance (see lag_sweep)
signed TRFs for N1/P2 latencies (validator stores GFP only)
per-condition split in the CLI (done here by filtering records before validate())
models.peak_shift should bound the parabolic step to +-1 sample and flag edge argmaxes (not changed here)
anomalies: aided S_014 trial 9 (first trial of its 2nd recording) peak-shift offset -19470 ms: estimator artefact (edge argmax + unbounded parabolic step in models.peak_shift); +-30 s sweep shows no tracking at any lag; inflates aided jitter_sd_ms to 1562 ms; MAD 13 ms
S_014 fails low in both conditions separately (aided p_mismatch 0.095; unaided r 0.023, p_circ 0.098) but passes pooled; notes.md reports large common artifacts in S_014 unaided
S_004 aided fails low (p_circ 0.059, r 0.025); S_004 unaided passes (r 0.069)
brainstem: no response (pooled SNR 0.99, p 0.45; unaided 0.97, p 0.77; 1/20 unaided subjects at p < 0.05, chance level); as expected from notes.md 7c
MLR GFP peak at 40-43 ms, near the upper edge of the 18-45 ms window

zero_lag_bump.question: secondary GFP bump at ~0 ms in the 0.5-8 Hz forward TRF (pooled GFP/null 4.6 vs 8.8 at 172 ms): autocorrelation or EEG leading the stimulus?
zero_lag_bump.method: zero_lag_bump.py, repo low-tier functions; per subject x condition: channel TRF, GFP(0 ms)/GFP(172 ms); synthetic control = EEG simulated from the TRF restricted to 100-300 ms lags, convolved with the real envelopes and refitted with the same ridge; topography correlation of the 0 ms and 172 ms maps

topography.note: same fronto-central positive / occipital negative pattern as the 172 ms map; no eye-like frontal-polar dominance (Fp1/Fp2/AF3/AF4 3% of power)

zero_lag_bump.trial_offsets_near_170ms: pooled run: 1/308 trials in -200..-140 ms, 3/308 in +140..+200 ms, 275/308 within +-50 ms (no subset of trials shifted by a P2 latency)
zero_lag_bump.conclusion: not autocorrelation/ridge smearing of the 172 ms peak (synthetic 0.03 vs 0.51 observed); present in nearly all subjects and both conditions, with the P2-like topography and no ocular pattern; the same 0 ms GFP level relative to the main peak (0.49-0.69) is seen in the hand-aligned reference datasets, so it is not specific to this dataset and gives no evidence of a timing error here; the repo check cannot say what the component is (it is a property of the EEG-envelope relation, e.g. a slow component spanning negative lags)

s014_aided_trial9.question: offset_s -19.47 for S_014 aided trial 9 (first trial of S_014's 2nd recording, odin_1_1)
s014_aided_trial9.estimator: artefact of models.peak_shift: the argmax of the +-0.5 s curve sits at the search edge (-0.5 s); np.clip moves the parabola centre to index 1, so the three points are not around a maximum, and with near-zero negative curvature the vertex step 0.5(a-c)/(a-2b+c) is unbounded. In the LOO re-fit (s014_sweep.py) the edge argmax is again -0.500 s and the curvature +1e-4 (no step), giving -0.484 s; the validator's 5-fold model gave a tiny negative curvature and the -19.47 s step

sweep_pm30s.method: s014_sweep.py: leave-one-trial-out model within condition, channel-summed cross-correlation of EEG and prediction at all shifts within +-30 s, normalised; z against |shift| > 2 s
sweep_pm30s.conclusion: trial 9 has no peak at any lag within +-30 s (its maximum is at noise level, like the far-lag maxima of every S_014 trial): no tracking, not a measurable misalignment

s014_aided_trial9.s014_other_offsets: the +-0.2-0.5 s offsets of S_014 trials (both conditions) coincide with z_at_0 < 2 and in-range argmaxes at noise peaks or the +-0.5 s edge: weak tracking (subject r 0.037 pooled; notes.md reports large artifacts in S_014 unaided), not trial misalignment
s014_aided_trial9.jitter_sd_without_artefact: use jitter_mad_ms (aided 13.1 ms); jitter_sd_ms is not robust to this estimator artefact
